sentences.sentence: A lung is an organ that exchanges gases between air and blood.
Bone is the hard tissue that forms the vertebrate skeleton.
Muscle is tissue that contracts to produce force and motion.
The eye is the organ that forms images from light.
The ear is the organ that detects sound and, in land vertebrates, helps with balance.
Skin is the outer barrier of the body; it limits water loss and infection.
Carbon is the element whose atoms form the backbone of organic molecules.
Oxygen is the element that makes up much of air and water and supports combustion and respiration.
Hydrogen is the lightest element and the most abundant in the universe.
Iron is a common metal and the main element in Earth's core and in steel.
Gold is a dense, unreactive yellow metal long used as money and ornament.
Silver is a white precious metal and an excellent electrical conductor.
Copper is a reddish metal used in wire because it conducts electricity well.
Silicon is the element used as the main semiconductor in most computer chips.
The periodic table arranges elements by atomic number and recurring chemical properties.
An acid is a substance that donates protons or raises hydronium concentration in water.
A base is a substance that accepts protons or raises hydroxide concentration in water.
In chemistry, a salt is an ionic compound formed from an acid and a base.
A crystal is a solid whose atoms sit on a repeating lattice.
Glass is an amorphous solid that flows only over geologic time.
A plastic is a moldable polymer material used for objects and films.
Petroleum is a fossil liquid of hydrocarbons used as fuel and chemical feedstock.
Coal is a carbon-rich sedimentary rock burned for heat and power.
Natural gas is a fossil fuel composed mainly of methane.
Nuclear fission splits heavy nuclei and releases energy used in reactors and weapons.
Nuclear fusion joins light nuclei; it powers stars and experimental reactors.
Radioactivity is the spontaneous decay of unstable nuclei with emission of particles or rays.
The electron is the light negative particle that occupies atoms and carries current in metals.
The proton is the positive nucleon that sets an element's atomic number.
The neutron is the uncharged nucleon that adds mass to the nucleus.
Quantum physics describes nature in discrete units of action, energy, and charge.
Relativity treats space and time as a single spacetime whose geometry is tied to mass-energy.
The speed of light in vacuum is a universal constant, about three hundred million meters per second.
A thermometer is an instrument that reports temperature on a chosen scale.
A calendar is a civil system for naming days, months, and years.
A clock is a machine that counts equal intervals and displays time of day.
A magnetic compass points along Earth's magnetic field and is used to find direction.
A telescope gathers light so distant objects can be seen or measured.
A microscope magnifies objects too small for the unaided eye.
The wheel and axle is a machine that turns sliding friction into rolling motion.
A lever is a rigid bar that turns on a fulcrum to multiply force or distance.
A heat engine converts a temperature difference into mechanical work.
An electric motor turns current and magnetic fields into rotation.
A generator converts mechanical rotation into electric current by induction.
A battery stores chemical energy and releases it as electric current.
An electric circuit is a closed path that current can follow.
Radio is wireless communication that uses electromagnetic waves below light.
A photograph is an image fixed by light on a sensitive surface or sensor.
Printing is the mechanical copying of text or image onto many sheets.
A book is a bound sequence of written or printed leaves meant to be read as one work.
